texts.0f375cac0c51f5c46f0a1bfc676887125142e3aa:
---
name: appworld-file-system-access
description: Use for AppWorld tasks that reference a file, receipt, bill, or document located "in my file system" (e.g. "~/bills/") whose data lives inside the simulated file_system app; confirm the app via metadata, skip host-shell find/ls probing, and read via the file_system API using supervisor credentials.
flashrsi:
  algorithm: evo_harness
  level: topic
  source_task_ids: [76f2c72_2, 3c13f5a_3]
---
When an AppWorld task references a file, receipt, bill, or document located "in my file system" (e.g. "~/bills/"):

1. Recognize that the data lives in the simulated `file_system` app, not the host shell. Host `ls`/`find` on such paths (e.g. `find / -iname '*bill*' -o -iname '*receipt*'`) returns nothing or "No such file or directory"; do not burn turns probing `/`, `/task`, `~`, `whoami`, or `echo $HOME`.
2. Run `metadata` up front to confirm `file_system` is among the available apps and to learn the exact call names.
3. Retrieve credentials from the supervisor: call `show_account_passwords` via the appworld client.
4. Read the relevant app docs: `docs file_system` (plus `docs supervisor`).
5. Read the file/directory through the file_system API (e.g. `show_directory`/`show_file`) using the retrieved access token.
6. Only then act on the returned contents as the task requests.

Trigger: if the session exposes AppWorld tools (appworld_client `metadata`/`docs`/`execute`) and a mentioned file/receipt/bill path is absent from the host filesystem, go straight to the app API instead of probing the shell.
texts.254a8a022439aaf5769342055bdf29ef5ae066e4:
---
name: appworld-api-doc-retrieval
description: Use for AppWorld/FlashRSI tasks where you need the signature of one or a few APIs from an app with a large API surface (e.g. Spotify); request docs for the specific API name instead of dumping the whole app, and avoid bundling several apps' docs into one call.
flashrsi:
  algorithm: evo_harness
  level: topic
  source_task_ids: [b0a8eae_1, b0a8eae_2]
---
When an AppWorld task spans an app that exposes many endpoints (e.g. Spotify) and you only need one or a few signatures:

1. Query the docs tool with a specific API name: `docs <app_name> <api_name>`. Whole-app `docs <app_name>` returns the entire API surface; for large apps this exceeds the output limit (observed 78KB and 91KB) and is persisted to a file with only a ~2KB preview shown, hiding the endpoint signature and wasting context.
2. Do not dump full docs for several apps in a single Bash call — combined output can cross the same limit, forcing a re-query and burning a scarce turn in a 30-turn budget.
3. Query one app at a time. When you must survey many endpoints, pipe docs through a compact filter that prints only api_name/method/path/short-description before reading full parameter details for the calls you actually need.

Trigger: when `docs <app_name>` returns an "Output too large" / persisted-output result, or before exploring a multi-app task, ask for the specific endpoint instead of the whole app.
texts.4419a4846b8c95710512b9ce689ae1039785811a:
---
name: appworld-api-doc-retrieval
description: Use for AppWorld/FlashRSI tasks where the session already lists flashrsi:* helper skills or where you need one or a few API signatures from an app with a large API surface (e.g. Spotify, Venmo); use a listed helper skill and request docs for the specific API name instead of dumping the whole app.
flashrsi:
  algorithm: evo_harness
  level: topic
  source_task_ids: [6ea6792_2]
---
When an AppWorld task lists flashrsi:* helper skills, or spans an app exposing many endpoints (e.g. Spotify, Venmo) while you only need a few signatures:

1. Check the available skills/slash_commands first. If a flashrsi:* helper already covers the app or task, use it instead of re-discovering the API by hand. Manual re-discovery — `metadata`, then whole-app `docs venmo` (46KB, persisted to file), then filtering and re-reading specific entries — burned the full 30-turn budget before any task action (login, list pending requests, deny each) occurred.
2. When you do need a signature, query the docs tool with a specific API name: `docs <app_name> <api_name>`. Whole-app `docs <app_name>` returns the entire API surface; for large apps this exceeds the output limit (observed 78KB and 91KB) and is persisted to a file with only a ~2KB preview shown, hiding the endpoint signature.
3. Do not dump full docs for several apps in a single Bash call. Query one app at a time; when surveying many endpoints, pipe docs through a compact filter that prints only api_name/method/path/short-description before reading full parameter details for the calls you actually need.

Trigger: when the session lists flashrsi:* helper skills for the app/task, or `docs <app_name>` returns an "Output too large" / persisted-output result — use the helper skill / ask for the specific endpoint instead of dumping the whole app.
texts.469a65578ac11298ec18eb3351195ca0f96c7245:
---
name: venmo-relationship-target-derivation
description: Use for AppWorld/Venmo tasks that mutate records qualified by a social relationship plus a time window (e.g. "payments I received from my friends"), where the target set must be derived by cross-referencing endpoints before bulk comment/like mutations.
flashrsi:
  algorithm: evo_harness
  level: topic
  source_task_ids: [afc0fce_2]
---
When a Venmo task requires acting on records qualified by a relationship (e.g. "payments I received from my friends"):

1. Do not assume the transactions endpoint exposes a friendship filter. `show_transactions` accepts only `user_email`, `direction`, and date/amount filters; there is no "friends" filter.
2. Enumerate the relationship set first with `search_friends`, which returns the friend emails.
3. Fetch candidate records with the appropriate filters: `show_transactions(direction='received', min_created_at=<simulated date - window>)`. Compute the date filter from the simulated datetime, inclusive of today.
4. Intersect the two result sets on the counterparty field (`sender.email`) to obtain the true target set.
5. Only after deriving the target set, apply the requested bulk mutation (e.g. comment/like) to those records.

Before mutating, verify the window boundary (inclusive of today) and confirm which counterparty field the intersection uses.

  level: topic

2. Retrieve credentials first from the supervisor: call `show_account_passwords` via the appworld client.
3. Read the relevant app docs up front: `docs file_system` (plus `docs supervisor`) and `metadata` to learn the exact call names.
4. Read the file/directory through the file_system API (e.g. `show_directory`/`show_file`) using the retrieved credentials.
5. Only then act on the returned contents as the task requests.

Trigger check: if the session exposes AppWorld tools (appworld_client `metadata`/`docs`/`execute`) and a mentioned path is absent from the host filesystem, go straight to the app API instead of probing the shell.
texts.a6013d39bb18a2469f1653f2b93410d35bac2a44:
---
name: appworld-api-doc-retrieval
description: Use for AppWorld/FlashRSI tasks where you need API signatures from a docs tool; request the specific API name instead of dumping the whole app, avoid bundling several apps' docs into one call, and after retrieving docs call only APIs whose exact names appear in them.
flashrsi:
  algorithm: evo_harness
  level: topic
  source_task_ids: [b0a8eae_1, b0a8eae_2, b0a8eae_3]
---
When an AppWorld task spans an app that exposes many endpoints (e.g. Spotify) and you only need one or a few signatures:

1. Query the docs tool with a specific API name: `docs <app_name> <api_name>`. Whole-app `docs <app_name>` returns the entire API surface; for large apps this exceeds the output limit (observed 78KB and 91KB) and is persisted to a file with only a ~2KB preview shown, hiding the endpoint signature and wasting context.
2. Do not dump full docs for several apps in a single Bash call — combined output can cross the same limit, forcing a re-query and burning a scarce turn in a 30-turn budget.
3. Query one app at a time. When you must survey many endpoints, pipe docs through a compact filter that prints only api_name/method/path/short-description before reading full parameter details for the calls you actually need.
4. After retrieving docs, call only APIs whose exact names appear in them. A fabricated helper (e.g. `show_note_system_info` on simple_note) fails with "No API named ..." and wastes a step; rely on documented endpoints (e.g. `search_notes` or `login` to obtain an access_token) instead of inventing helpers.

Trigger: when `docs <app_name>` returns an "Output too large" / persisted-output result, before exploring a multi-app task, or before calling an API after fetching its docs — verify the exact endpoint name against the documentation.
